evidence: src/application/catalogue-service.ts: CatalogueService.create and listStock both return results through toProductDto from ./dtos and save and read through ProductRepository.
src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService.place, advance, cancel and listByStatus all return results through toOrderDto from ./dtos and persist through OrderRepository.
src/application/dtos.ts: toOrderDto and toProductDto are the only places domain entities are converted to DTOs; both services use them.

src/application/order-service.ts: stock reservation and release go through the domain StockReservationService.reserve/release and are not reimplemented here; the not-found check exists only in requireOrder.
src/application/dtos.ts: the line shape { productId: string; quantity: number } is written out in both PlaceOrderInput and OrderDto. This is minor type repetition, not a duplicated rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module passes as one coherent unit: a set of use-case services for a single order and catalogue context, plus their shared input/output types (DTOs). Both services follow the same pattern. Each one takes a domain repository in its constructor, does its work through domain entities and services, and converts results with the shared mappers in dtos.ts. Neither service builds DTOs inline, so the module's own mapping helpers are never bypassed. Each rule lives in one place. Stock reservation and release live in the domain StockReservationService. The order not-found check is a single private helper, OrderService.requireOrder. Product-to-DTO and order-to-DTO conversion each live in one function in dtos.ts. Two small points don't change the result. First, the line shape { productId, quantity } is written out twice in dtos.ts, once in PlaceOrderInput and once in OrderDto. That repeats a type, not a rule. Second, OrderService creates its StockReservationService inside its constructor instead of having it passed in. That is a choice about how dependencies are supplied, not a split in what the module does or a bypass of its abstractions.
